full_judgment: 3. Defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the contentions made in the plaint. His case was that the C.S. tenants abandoned the jote and the landlords of Ambaria Estate took possession of the same as their khas lands and possessed the same for some time and thereafter settled the suit land with defendant No. 1 in the year 1348 B.S. and since then the defendant has possessed the suit lands. He has sold a portion of the suit land to the predecessor of defendant Nos. 2 to 4 about 20 years ago. The records of rights have been correctly prepared in the names of the defendants. Bancharam Kaiborta, son of Lakshan Kaiborta left for India about 40 years ago. So according to the defendant, the kabala of the plaintiff is false and fabricated. The defendants are the owners of the suit land and they have possessed the same and that the plaintiff has got no right, title and possession over the same. The suit was, therefore, liable to be dismissed with costs.
